state.case_summary:
An 80-year-old woman presented with involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs for more than 10 days. She had a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus. On neurological examination, she had a slow response, reduced muscle strength, and positive tendon reflexes in her left limbs. Continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude were observed in the left arm and leg. Laboratory testing revealed a blood glucose level of 8.59 mmol/L (reference range, 3.9–6.1) and a hemoglobin A1c of 7.43% (4–6), with all other laboratory values within normal limits. Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions without evidence of acute infarction. Subsequent brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia.
